la:verb:intro.gloss: to enter, go into, come in, get in, penetrate
senses: to enter, go into, come in, get in, penetrate
la:verb:intro.html:
intrō, adv.
contr. from interō sc. loco
.
Inwardly, internally; on the inside: omnia sana faciet, intro quae dolitabunt,: stare,; ; cf. .—
To the inside, within, in (class.): sequere intro me, amabo,into the house,: intro ad nos venit,: intro ire,: intro advenire,: abire,: intro est itum,: cur ad nos filiam tuam non intro vocari jubes?; cf.: prius quam intro vocarentur ad suffragium tribus,; so, intro vocata centuria,: accipere,.

la:prep:intra.html:
intrā, adv. and prep.
contr. from intĕrā; sc. parte
,
on the inside, within (class. only as a prep.).
Adv. (post-Aug.).
In gen.: quadraginta per oram, intra centum erunt,: pars, quae intra, longior esse debet, quam quae extra,: si inciditur, viridis intra caro apparet,: vasa extrinsecus, et intra diligenter picata,.—
Esp.
Of the interior of countries: intra vix jam homines magisque semiferi, Mela, 1, 4, 4.—
Of the interior of a building: pro rostris aurata aedes ... intraque lectus eburneus,: intra forisque,.—
Of the Mediterranean Sea, Mela, prooem. 2: abunde orbe terrae extra intra indicato (opp. extra, of the ocean),—
Inwardly, towards the inside (rare): binos interim digitos distinguimus ... paulum tamen inferioribus intra spectantibus, Quint. 11, 3, 98.—
Prep. with acc. (placed after its noun: praeturam intra,, and: lucem intra,), within.
Lit., of place: intra navim,: intra parietes meos,: carceres stare,: jactum teli, within a javelin's throw, : montem Taurum,: locus intra oceanum jam, nullus est, quo non, etc.,: Apenninum,: ea intra se consumunt Arabes,consume among themselves, in their own country,: Sy. Devoravi nomen inprudens modo. Ch. Non placet qui amicos intra dentis conclusos habet, behind, ; cf.: inter dentis, Brix.—
Transf.
I. q. in with acc., in, into: ea intra pectus se penetravit potio,: nosse regiones, intra quas venere,: qui intra fines suos Ariovistum recepissent,: intra moenia compulsus,.—
Of time, within, during, in the course of, in less than: intra viginti dies,: qui intra annos quatuordecim tectum non subiissent,: quae intra decem annos facta sunt, (dub.; B. and K. inter): intra paucos dies,; : intra breve tempus,; : juventam,in youth,. — With quam ( = postquam): intra decimum diem quam Pheras venerat,i. e. before the lapse of ten days after his arrival,; ; ; —
Trop.
Under, below, i. e. less than, fewer than, within the limits of: intra centum,: epulari intra legem,i. e. less expensively than the law allows,: intra modum,: intra verba desipere,to betray insanity in words only,: intra verba peccare,to transgress in words only,: intra gloriam fuit facinus,i. e. was not inglorious,: intra silentium se tenere,to keep silence,: intra famam sunt scripta,beneath his reputation,: intra fortunam,.—
With acc. of pron., within or among.
Intra se, inwardly, to one's self: meditantes intra semet,: intra se dicere,: intra se componere,.—
Secretly: intra vos futura,shall remain among yourselves, be kept secret,.

la:verb:introduco.gloss: to lead in: to conduct into
senses: to lead in: to conduct into
la:verb:introduco.html:
intrō-dūco, duxi, ductum, 3, v. a.,
to lead or bring into a place, to conduct into or within (syn.: induco, immitto).
Lit.
With acc.: gregem venalium,: noctu milites,: Volturcium cum legatis,: praesidium,; cf. se,: aliquem tecum,: quod oppidum cohortibus introductis tenebat,.—
With in and acc.: si suas copias Aedui in fines Bellovacorum introduxerint,: legationes in senatum,: in senatum aliquem ad agendas gratias,: praesidium in urbem Chium,.—
With ad and acc.: ad regem,. —
With eo: nacti portum, eo naves introduxerunt,.—
Trop.
To bring in, introduce: philosophiam in domos,: aliquem in possessionem,: ambitionem in senatum,to introduce,; : senatusconsulta,. —
Esp., in speaking or writing, to introduce a person or subject: Catonem senem disputantem,: sermones,: fictam narrationem,; cf.: pictores animas sensibus auctas,represented,.—
To bring forward, maintain: non modo natum mundum introduxit, sed etiam paene manu factum,: introducebat, summum bonum esse, frui,: deliberationem,: narrationem,—
To institute, originate: ex hujus modi principio consuetudo aestimationis introducta est,: hac introducta consuetudine,: ejusmodi deliberationem,: consuetudinem,: novum in republica exemplum,to set an example,: exemplum a patricio homine introductum,: leges perniciosissimas reipublicae,: ritus novos,: novas superstitiones,.

la:verb:introeo.html:
intro-ĕo (ante-class. introdeo;
introiet for introibit,), īvi, or ĭi, ĭtum, 4, v. n., to go in or into, to enter (syn.: intro, ingredior); constr. with in or ad and acc., with acc., with in and abl., with inf.
Lit.
With in and acc.: vereri introdire in alienam domum,: in urbem,; : in domum,: in Thraciam,: in tabernaculum,.—
With ad: ad amicam,: sicuti salutatum introire ad Ciceronem,.—
With acc.: domum,: curiam,: urbem,: theatrum,: castra,: Syracusas,: Bithyniam,.—
With in and abl. (ante-class.): in naso, .—(ε) With inf.: filius introiit videre, quid agat,went in to see,.—(ζ) With huc, .— Impers.: cum periculo introitur recenti apertione,: castra sine vulnere introitum, entered, ap. . —
Trop.: quem fuerat aequius, ut prius introieram, sic prius exire de vita,.

la:adj:intractabilis.html:
in-tractābĭlis, e, adj.,
not to be handled or meddled with, unmanageable, intractable; rough, rude, wild, fierce (since the Aug. per.): genus intractabile bello,; cf. in comp.: homo naturā intractabilior et morosior,.— Of inanim. and abstr. things: pastinacae virus intractabile est,: loca frigore,uninhabitable,: intractabilis et dura aetas,: bruma,: ira,.

la:verb:intremo.html:
in-trĕmo, ŭi, 3, v. n. and a.
Neutr., to tremble, shake, quake: totum corpus intremit,: omnem Murmure Trinacriam,: intremuit malus,; so, tellus,: quercus,: genua intremuere,; 2, 180: quo (clamore) intremuere undae,.—
Act., to tremble at or before: regum eventus,: Hannibalem,.

la:adj:intractatus.html:
in-tractātus, a, um, adj.
2. in-tracto
,
not handled or managed, untamed, wild; untried, unattempted (class.): equus,unbroken,: decor,wild, natural, simple,: lanae,not carded,: ne quid intractatum scelerisve dolive fuisset,.

la:adj:intrepidus.html:
in-trĕpĭdus, a, um, adj.
2. in
,
unshaken, undaunted, intrepid (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Of living beings: intrepidus minantibus,: paucae bestiarum in hostem actae,: dux,: tranquillus, intrepidus, immobilis,: genitor discrimine nati,: nova nupta,: fortis et intrepidus,: ac paratus,; ; , ext. 3; Plin. praef. § 5; : quaecumque altaria tangere,—With Gr. acc.: voltum,.—
Of inanim. and abstr. things: vultus,: modulatio,that drives away fear,: verba,: hiems,i. e. spent in quiet winter-quarters, without disturbance from enemies,.— Adv.: intrĕpĭdē, without trembling, undauntedly, intrepidly, ; ; ; ; .

la:verb:intromitto.gloss: to send or let in or into; to admit
senses: to send or let in or into; to admit
la:verb:intromitto.html:
intrō-mitto, mīsi, missum, 3, v. a. (
inf. pass. intromittier, ), to send in, to let in or into (syn. induco, immitto; class.).
Lit., with in and acc.: lepores in leporarium,; cf.: legiones (sc. in oppidum),: Caninium legatum,: in aedes,: qui cum bestiis in harenam intromissi sunt,.— With two acc.: sex milia peditum Nolam intromisit,.— With ad: quemquam ad vos,: ad Senecam aliquem,. —With sup.: Phaedriam comissatum,. —
Trop., to introduce (post-class.): verba in usum linguae Latinae,: exemplum,: controversiam (εἰσάγεσθαι δίκην), .

la:noun:introitus.gloss: a going in or into, entering; an entrance
senses: a going in or into, entering; an entrance
a place of entrance; passage; mouth of a river
an entering or entrance into an office or a society; entrance fee
la:noun:introitus.html:
intrŏĭtus, ūs, m.
introeo
,
a going in or into, an entering, entrance (class.).
Lit.: nocturnus introitus Zmyrnam quasi in hostium urbem,: militum,: in urbem,: sol in Geminos introitum facit,enters,: primo statim introitu,at his very first entrance,: aliquem introitu prohibere,: cujus in Graeciam,: introitum alicujus rei pellere,to keep a thing from entering,.—With in and abl. (rare): sol introitum in Cancro facit,.—
Esp., the mouth of a river, its entrance into another: Averni,; also as the entrance to it from the sea (cf. B. infra): Indi, —
Transf., a place of entrance, passage: ad omnes introitus, qua adiri poterat,: omnes introitus erant praeclusi,: clandestinus,: aures duros et quasi corneolos habere introitus,: portus,; : aedis,: ad ipsum introitum exspectare macelli,. —In the abl.: INTROITO,. —
Trop.
An entering, entrance upon an office or into a society: certum aliquid pro introitu dare,: sacerdotii,: militiam illam cum introitu comparari volo,i. e. entrancemoney,.—
A beginning, introduction, prelude (syn.: principium, exordium, prooemium): fabulae Clodianae,: defensionis,: in introitu hujus operis,.
